issues.title: Nature of ARD offers
issues.author: jariarkko
issues.body:
Introduction says:

"Agent Resource Discovery (ARD) [[ARD](https://jaime.win/ietf-draft-ard-initial-contact/draft-jimenez-ard-initial-contact.html#ARD)] defines a catalog of agent resources, a document served over HTTPS in which a publisher lists the agents, tool servers, and skills it offers."

I wonder if the right term would be "knows about". Is there an "offer" in this context? What if the directory server simply crawled potential resources and lists them, can we say it "offers" a resource?

I had several question marks here

2. I can't quite put my finger on it, but I have some unease with the way we specify these different kinds of initial contacts. (This was the same when I read the original ARD docs.) 2. Is a configured entry point a domain name or a URI? I.e., do you go direct to the configured one or apply the rest of the rules for using SVCB etc.?

3.  Is there a "don't look at others" rule somewhere, eg. as with the above corporate agent server example?

4. On bullet item 3, is "browse" the right term in "The client browses _ard._tcp.D (Section 4.4.3)."?

5. The first paragraph after the list appears like an action, should it be on the list? "A client without a domain name browses "_ard._tcp.local." over Multicast DNS (Section 4.5.2)."

3. Do we do the .well-known optional? I mean we could expand on the static configurations too.

issues.title: Support both static entry sources (_entries._agents) and dynamic registry endpoints (_search._agents)
issues.author: mindpower
issues.body:
Currently the draft assumes that initial discovery always resolves to a static catalog document (`/.well-known/ard.json`), and that the lookup API is always discovered through a static catalog first:

- **Section 1 (line 131):** *"Agent Resource Discovery (ARD) {{ARD}} defines a catalog of agent resources, a document served over HTTPS... ARD also defines a lookup interface over the catalog. Both require the URI of the catalog."*
- **Section 3 (lines 176–177):** *"URI: The "https" URI {{RFC9110}} of the catalog. Retrieving it returns an ARD catalog in a representation defined by {{ARD}}."*
- **Section 4.2.1 (lines 204–221):** Only defines `_catalog._agents.<domain>` pointing to `/.well-known/ard.json`.
- **Section 5 (line 333):** *"An entry point fails if the server does not respond, if the response is not a catalog, or if the checks of {{security}} fail."*

In ARD (`ard-spec` Section 5.1 and `draft-bu-agent-resources-discovery` Section 3), a domain or registry operator does not have to host a static `ard.json` file in order to run a dynamic ARD Registry (`POST /search`, `POST /explore`, `GET /entries`). A client can be configured with or discover a dynamic registry endpoint directly, or a crawler/client can discover a static manifest (`ard.json` or `ai-catalog.json`).

### Suggested updates

1. **Two DNS pointer labels in Section 4.2.1 (matching `ard-spec` Section 5.1):**
   - **Static entry source (`_entries._agents.<domain>`):** Points to a static entries document (`/.well-known/ard.json` or `/.well-known/ai-catalog.json`). Using `_entries._agents.<domain>` (also mentioned in Open Issue #2, line 457) works cleanly across both `ard.json` and `ai-catalog.json` since both formats use a top-level `entries` array.
   - **Dynamic registry endpoint (`_search._agents.<domain>`):** Points directly to an ARD Registry base URL (where the client invokes `/search`, `/explore`, or `/entries`).

2. **Entry point definition (Section 3 & Section 5):**
   - Update Section 3 (line 177), Section 4.1 (Configured Entry Points, line 194), and Section 5 (line 333) so an entry point can identify either:
     - a static manifest/catalog document (`application/ard+json`), or
     - a dynamic ARD Registry API endpoint.

comments.author: jaimejim
comments.body: I'd leave this for -01. Making an entry point a registry endpoint changes the entry point definition, step 2, the failure rule and the ranking, and we agreed to keep -00 minimal. It is also close to the search side that Mirja flagged as the edge of the charter. For now the open issues list records the `_search._agents` pointer and the question (https://github.com/jaimejim/ietf-draft-ard-initial-contact/pull/20); `_entries._agents` was already in open issue 2.

issues.title: Align draft name, per-entry publisher check, and ard spec
issues.author: mindpower
issues.body:
A few smaller alignment items from reviewing `draft-jimenez-ard-initial-discovery.md` alongside `draft-bu-agent-resources-discovery` (PR #31) and `ard-spec`:

1. **Keep draft filename / `docname` as `draft-jimenez-ard-initial-contact` (lines 6, 24):**
   - Per our discussion, let's keep the draft name as `draft-jimenez-ard-initial-contact` (matching the repo name and the `-00` submission on Datatracker) rather than renaming the file/`docname` to `draft-jimenez-ard-initial-discovery`. (Keeping the title *"Agent Resource Discovery (ARD): Initial Discovery"* is fine.)

2. **Update `ARD` reference author list (lines 58–67):**
   - Add Jari Arkko (Ericsson) and Jeffrey Damick (Amazon) to the author list for `draft-bu-agent-resources-discovery`.

3. **Distinguish domain owner (container level) vs. entry publisher (Section 3 line 182, Section 6.1 line 357, Section 6.4 line 371):**
   - Line 182 says *"The publisher of a catalog is established by the catalog content, as specified in {{ARD}}"* and line 357 says *"the recorded source is the input to the publisher check that {{ARD}} defines."*
   - In `{{ARD}}`, a catalog or registry can contain entries from multiple publishers, and publisher verification is performed **per entry** against the `<publisher>` domain in `urn:air:<publisher>:...` (via the entry's `trustManifest` signature or same-origin HTTPS when fetched from `https://<publisher>/.well-known/ard.json`), optionally alongside any container-level signature from the `<domain>` owner (such as when a catalog is served from an off-domain target via DNS).

4. **Appendix A `ARD-SPEC` description (line 446):**
   - Line 446 states that `{{ARD-SPEC}}` *"publishes an SVCB record at `_ard._tcp.<domain>`"*. `ard-spec` Section 5.1 only lists `_entries._agents` and `_search._agents` (the `_ard._tcp` SVCB example was only in an earlier version of `draft-bu`).

5. **Open Issue #4 (line 459 — Ownership of registrations):**
   - We removed the duplicate `ard.json` Well-Known URI and `ard` Link Relation IANA registrations from `draft-bu-agent-resources-discovery` (PR #31) and deferred them to this draft, so Open Issue #4 can be closed/removed.

issues.title: Web crawler discovery mechanisms and ai-catalog fallback
issues.author: mindpower
issues.body:
In `ard-spec` Section 5.1 (and AI Catalog), initial discovery is used not only by runtime clients resolving a domain, but also by registry web crawlers ingesting published manifests. A few mechanisms from `ard-spec` Section 5.1 are currently missing or only partially covered in `draft-jimenez-ard-initial-discovery.md`:

1. **HTML `<link rel="ard">` in Section 4.3.2 (`#link-relation`, lines 285–303):**
   - Currently Section 4.3.2 only describes the HTTP `Link` response header on `HEAD /`.
   - Since RFC 8288 link relations also apply to HTML `<link>` elements, `ard-spec` Section 5.1 includes `<link rel="ard" href="...">` in the HTML `<head>` so web crawlers and publishers who cannot set custom HTTP headers (e.g., on static hosting) can still link to their manifest.

2. **`robots.txt` `Agentmap:` directive (`ard-spec` Section 5.1):**
   - `ard-spec` Section 5.1 defines an `Agentmap:` directive in `robots.txt` (e.g., `Agentmap: https://example.com/entries.json`, analogous to `Sitemap:`) so web crawlers can locate the manifest when a publisher cannot serve it at `/.well-known/ard.json`.

3. **Optional compatibility fallback for `/.well-known/ai-catalog.json` and `rel="ai-catalog"` (`ard-spec` Section 5.1):**
   - `ard-spec` Section 5.1 notes that while `/.well-known/ard.json` and `rel="ard"` are the normative requirements, a consumer or crawler MAY additionally consult `/.well-known/ai-catalog.json` and `rel="ai-catalog"` as compatible entry sources (with `ard.json` taking precedence if both exist). Mentioning this in Section 4.3 (or Appendix A) keeps the draft aligned with `ard-spec`.

comments.author: jaimejim
comments.body:
1. Done, in https://github.com/jaimejim/ietf-draft-ard-initial-contact/pull/20.
2. I'd keep this out. robots.txt is for crawlers, and RFC 9309 lets them read extra records, so the ARD draft's ingestion section is the right home for Agentmap. Here it would be one more mechanism while we are trying to have fewer (#6).
3. Also out, I think. This document registers ard.json and cannot ask clients to try an unregistered path as well. Compatibility with ai-catalog.json is an ARD-side matter.

issues.author: jaimejim
issues.body:
Removed from -00 in PR #23 (pre-submission review, item M2).

Section 3.2.2 let the HTTPS record of a domain announce the `ard.json` suffix through the `well-known` SvcParamKey of draft-mk-dnsop-svcb-well-known. That key has no IANA number yet, and its value syntax (suffix vs. full path) and wire encoding (length-prefixed list vs. single string) are open issues in that draft; the designated experts asked for HTTPBIS consultation before a renewed allocation. The draft keeps a sentence in Related Work and an entry in Open Issues. Re-add the section in a later -xx once the key has a number, a syntax and an example that loads into a zone.

pulls.title: Five consistency fixes from a read-through: mDNS targets, ranking constraints, link relation, HTTPS record, small items
pulls.author: jaimejim
pulls.body:
Five fixes found while reading the draft against itself and against RFC 6762, RFC 6763, and RFC 9460. One commit per item.

- Multicast DNS: a unicast SRV target is resolved through unicast DNS, and address records for it in a multicast answer are ignored. A Multicast DNS responder is authoritative only for names under "local." (RFC 6762, Section 6), and RFC 6762 Section 3 declines to specify resolution of global names over multicast. The earlier text let the client use those records.
- Procedure: the ranking stays a RECOMMENDED default. Local policy may reorder, except that configured entry points are tried first and entry points learned over Multicast DNS MUST rank last. This aligns the procedure with the unconditional rule in the configured entry points section and the MUST in the local network security section.
- Link relation: the SHOULD on the root HEAD response is conditioned on the publisher supporting the mechanism, matching the wording of the well-known section. The mechanism is OPTIONAL for publishers.
- HTTPS record at the apex: the "well-known" key indicates that the publisher serves a catalog at the well-known URI. The earlier text said the client could determine that the fetch will succeed, which a DNS record cannot promise.
- Three small items: the abstract and introduction now say the HTTPS record is at the apex rather than under "_agents"; the well-known section no longer duplicates the caching MUST of the procedure; the "mandatory" key is described before the ignored-keys rule in the pointer record bullets.

No change to the Open Issues section, registrations, or examples. `make lint`, prose-lint over all added lines, and the txt build pass.

Stacked on #9; retargets to main when that merges.
